data.description:
## The defect

`test.yml`'s `concurrency` group makes the 6-hourly SCHEDULED run and any manual
`workflow_dispatch` on `main` mutually cancelling. Whichever starts second kills the first. Because
main's health signal is **only** the scheduled run — `main` is deliberately excluded from the push
trigger — a cancelled scheduled run means **no main-health reading until the next 6-hour boundary**.

The workflow's own comment states the intent: the branch-health signal is "is main healthy NOW",
not "was every commit green". A silent cancellation defeats exactly that.

## It happened TWICE in one day

```
33874909241  main 69cd2b9e1  schedule           CANCELLED  12:51:27
33875177644  main 1af450654  workflow_dispatch  success    12:54:34   <- cancelled the 12:51 schedule

33905162633  main ee2c54f88  workflow_dispatch  CANCELLED  18:18:15   <- killed by the 18:45 schedule
33907581465  main cfff861c0  schedule           running    18:45:19
```

The first cost a scheduled reading entirely. The second cost a manual reading that had already
produced five confirmed job failures and was cancelled mid-flight, taking `sweep (macos, full
suite)` down with it before it could report.

## Why it is worth fixing rather than just knowing

The cancellation is SILENT in the only place anyone looks. `gh run list` shows `cancelled`, which
reads as "someone stopped it", not as "main's health is now unknown for up to six hours". An
operator or agent asking "is main green?" sees a cancelled run and has no signal that the answer is
unavailable rather than merely interrupted.

It also creates a perverse incentive: an agent wanting an on-demand reading near a 6-hour boundary
will destroy the scheduled reading to get it, or lose its own — and cannot tell in advance which,
because the cron carries jitter (nominal minute 41; the 18:45 run fired four minutes late).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1 — A manual `workflow_dispatch` of `test.yml` on `main` and the scheduled run no longer
      cancel one another. Whatever the mechanism (a concurrency group keyed to include the event or
      the sha, `cancel-in-progress: false` for this lane, or refusing a redundant dispatch), BOTH
      readings must be obtainable.
- [ ] AC2 — Redundant work is still bounded. This must not become "every dispatch queues another
      full sweep", which is the cost the concurrency group exists to control. State explicitly what
      the new bound is.
- [ ] AC3 — When a main-health run IS cancelled or superseded for any reason, that fact is
      distinguishable from "main is unhealthy" and from "main is healthy" — a reader must be able to
      tell that the signal is UNAVAILABLE. Absence of a reading must not present as either outcome.
- [ ] AC4 — Reproduce the collision (dispatch near a schedule boundary) and demonstrate both runs
      surviving, or the dispatch being refused with a clear reason. A fix not exercised against the
      real collision has not been shown to work.

## Non-goals

Not re-enabling the push trigger on `main` — it is excluded for a documented and good reason (on
`main`, `github.ref` is the constant `refs/heads/main`, so every push cancelled its predecessor and
GitHub rendered a healthy main as a trail of red X's). Not changing what the sweep lanes test.
data.title: Scheduled and manually-dispatched test.yml runs on main mutually cancel, so a collision silently leaves main-health unknown for up to 6 hours
